Cash Permission BandsLink

Permission bandConditionFounder postureRequired control action
Cash-permittedCollection proof, release posture, and outgoing funding sequence are current and aligned.Movement can proceed inside approved limits.Record owner, route, and next review date.
Cash-containedMovement is strategically valid but depends on near-term collection or release proof.Keep movement narrow and reversible.Require collections, credit, funding, and capital support before widening.
Cash-watchForecast is acceptable, but timing, concentration, or margin quality remains sensitive.Allow planning but not expansion.Refresh source records before commitment language strengthens.
Cash-constrainedStress gap or release-dependent exposure exceeds tolerance.Prioritize liquidity over growth pressure.Route to capital allocation, risk register, and founder decisions.
Cash-blockedMovement would widen exposure without collection proof, release control, or downside response.Stop movement until proof changes.Record blocked action and recovery trigger.

Collections Proof StandardLink

Proof typeMinimum evidenceWeak substitute to rejectFounder read
Customer promiseNamed contact, amount, date, follow-up owner, and next escalation step.General verbal comfort.A promise is forecastable only when it has owner and date discipline.
Receivable qualityAging status, dispute posture, credit posture, and release dependency.A clean invoice without payment behavior context.Cash quality depends on friction, not invoice value alone.
Release dependencyRelease gate, blocked action, deposit logic, and next permissible move.Operations urgency or relationship rationale.Release should follow cash proof, not create cash dependency.
Cash concentrationTop-account share, linked exposure, and mitigation action.Aggregate cash total without customer concentration read.Liquidity is weaker when it depends on one account.
Margin qualityProfitability review, concession path, and realized economics.Gross inflow without margin or recovery check.Cash is healthier when margin quality is visible.

Founder Release and Funding GatesLink

GateRequired evidenceIf evidence is currentIf evidence is weak
Collection gateCollections control and customer receivable record show amount, date, owner, and escalation path.Allow cash-permitted or cash-contained movement.Keep release narrow and escalate follow-up.
Credit and release gateCredit posture, blocked actions, deposit logic, and release conditions are current.Permit movement only inside the approved boundary.Block widening until credit and release records refresh.
Funding gateFunding and payables review shows priority, timing, and cash sequence.Release outgoing cash according to founder order.Hold non-critical funding until sequence is reconciled.
Capital allocation gateCapital review confirms scarce cash, release, and capacity support.Align movement with top priority items only.Reallocate or pause lower-priority movement.
Risk and scenario gateScenario response and risk register show containment path.Proceed with monitored downside plan.Treat cash movement as blocked or constrained.

Escalation and Stop RulesLink

RuleConditionRequired escalationFounder action
Collection slip stopA top-account promise slips or loses owner/date clarity.Route to collections, customer account, cash forecast, and risk register.Downgrade cash confidence and restrict release expansion.
Release exposure stopRelease-dependent cash remains above threshold or widens.Route to credit release, funding release, and capital allocation.Hold non-priority movement until exposure falls.
Stress gap triggerDownside gap remains above USD 50,000 or expands.Route to scenario response and founder decisions.Pre-sequence containment and delay optional outflows.
Pricing exception cash triggerA pricing exception weakens margin or inflow quality.Route to pricing governance and trade profitability.Block cash-quality reliance until recovery path exists.
Outgoing funding conflictShipment or payables request outruns collection proof.Route to funding release and capital allocation.Approve only top-priority funding or hold.
